 │     1 # Algorithm Documentation: Rust Code to RDF Ontology Generation                                                            │
 │     2                                                                                                                            │
 │     3 This document details the algorithm employed by the prepare_sources tool to analyze Rust source code, extract semantic   │
 │       information, transform it into a Clifford algebra representation, map it to emojis, and finally generate an RDF ontology.  │
 │     4                                                                                                                            │
 │     5 ## 1. Overall Purpose                                                                                                      │
 │     6                                                                                                                            │
 │     7 The primary goal of this algorithm is to bridge the gap between Rust source code and a semantic, machine-readable          │
 │       representation in the form of an RDF (Resource Description Framework) ontology. This ontology captures the structural and  │
 │       semantic essence of Rust functions, their relationships to files, and their conceptual proximity to a predefined           │
 │       emoji-based semantic space.                                                                                                │
 │     8                                                                                                                            │
 │     9 ## 2. Key Steps and Components                                                                                             │
 │    10                                                                                                                            │
 │    11 The algorithm proceeds through several distinct stages, leveraging various Rust crates for specialized tasks:              │
 │    12                                                                                                                            │
 │    13 ### 2.1. Project Analysis (project_analyzer.rs)                                                                          │
 │    14                                                                                                                            │
 │    15 This module orchestrates the entire analysis process.                                                                      │
 │    16 *   **File Discovery**: It begins by recursively scanning the specified project root directory to identify all Rust        │
 │       source files (.rs extension) using the walkdir crate.                                                                  │
 │    17 *   **Function Extraction**: For each Rust file found, it invokes the analyze_rust_file function from                    │
 │       function_analyzer.rs.                                                                                                    │
 │    18 *   **Error Handling**: Gracefully handles errors during file reading or parsing, logging the issues and skipping          │
 │       problematic files without crashing the entire process.                                                                     │
 │    19 *   **Progress Indication**: Utilizes the indicatif crate to display a dynamic progress bar, providing visual feedback   │
 │       during the potentially long analysis of large codebases.                                                                   │
 │    20                                                                                                                            │
 │    21 ### 2.2. Rust Code Parsing and Semantic Summary Extraction (function_analyzer.rs)                                        │
 │    22                                                                                                                            │
 │    23 This module is responsible for dissecting Rust files.                                                                      │
 │    24 *   **Syntax Parsing**: It uses the syn crate to parse the Rust source code into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).          │
 │    25 *   **Function Identification**: It iterates through the AST to identify and extract individual function definitions (     │
 │       syn::Item::Fn).                                                                                                          │
 │    26 *   **Code Snippet Capture**: For each function, it captures the raw code snippet using the quote crate.                 │
 │    27 *   **Semantic Summary Generation**: The extract_semantic_summary function generates a simplified semantic               │
 │       representation of the function. Currently, this involves concatenating the function's identifier, input arguments, and     │
 │       return type. This summary serves as the input for the embedding model.                                                     │
 │    28 *   **Path Normalization**: Ensures that file paths are normalized to use forward slashes (/) for consistency across     │
 │       different operating systems (e.g., Windows backslashes are replaced).                                                      │
 │    29                                                                                                                            │
 │    30 ### 2.3. BERT Embedding Generation (embedding.rs)                                                                        │
 │    31                                                                                                                            │
 │    32 This module converts textual semantic summaries into high-dimensional numerical vectors.                                   │
 │    33 *   **Model Retrieval**: It fetches the sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 BERT model and its associated tokenizer   │
 │       from the Hugging Face Hub (hf-hub crate).                                                                                │
 │    34 *   **Tokenization**: The tokenizers crate is used to tokenize the semantic_summary into numerical token_ids and     │
 │       attention_mask.                                                                                                          │
 │    35 *   **Input Truncation**: It truncates the tokenized input to the BERT model's maximum sequence length (                   │
 │       max_position_embeddings, typically 512) to prevent out-of-bounds errors.                                                 │
 │    36 *   **Model Inference**: The candle machine learning framework is used to load the BERT model weights and perform a      │
 │       forward pass, generating a 384-dimensional embedding vector for the input text.                                            │
 │    37 *   **Mean Pooling**: Aggregates the token-level embeddings into a single sentence-level embedding using mean pooling.     │
 │    38                                                                                                                            │
 │    39 ### 2.4. Clifford Multivector Conversion (clifford.rs)                                                                   │
 │    40                                                                                                                            │
 │    41 This module transforms the BERT embeddings into a Clifford algebra representation.                                         │
 │    42 *   **`BertCliffordEncoder`**: This custom encoder takes the 384-dimensional BERT embedding and projects it into an        │
 │       8-dimensional Clifford algebra multivector (SolMultivector).                                                             │
 │    43 *   **Projection Matrix**: A randomly initialized projection matrix (8x384) is used to map the high-dimensional BERT       │
 │       space to the 8-dimensional generator space of the Clifford algebra.                                                        │
 │    44 *   **`tclifford` Crate**: The tclifford crate is used to define the 8D Clifford algebra (SolCl) and perform           │
 │       multivector operations.                                                                                                    │
 │    45                                                                                                                            │
 │    46 ### 2.5. Sieve Addressing (sieve.rs)                                                                                     │
 │    47                                                                                                                            │
 │    48 This module generates a unique binary address for each multivector.                                                        │
 │    49 *   **Sign-Based Addressing**: For each 8-dimensional multivector, an 8-bit binary "sieve address" is generated based on   │
 │       the sign (positive or negative) of its 8 basis vector components. A positive component maps to '1', and a negative         │
 │       component maps to '0'.                                                                                                     │
 │    50                                                                                                                            │
 │    51 ### 2.6. Emoji Mapping and Ontology Integration (project_analyzer.rs, load_emoji_multivectors.rs)                      │
 │    52                                                                                                                            │
 │    53 This stage connects the numerical representations to a semantic emoji space.                                               │
 │    54 *   **Emoji Ontology Loading**: The load_emoji_multivectors function reads an existing RDF ontology (e.g.,               │
 │       ontologies/zos/v1.ttl) that defines a semantic space of emojis, each associated with a BERT embedding and a category.    │
 │    55 *   **Closest Emoji Calculation**: For each analyzed function's multivector:                                               │
 │    56     *   It calculates the Euclidean distance to all emoji multivectors in the loaded ontology.                             │
 │    57     *   It identifies the 3 closest emojis, along with their categories and distances.                                     │
 │    58     *   If a semantic summary is already present in the ontology, it uses that mapping directly.                           │
 │    59 *   **`AnalyzedFunction` Enrichment**: The AnalyzedFunction struct is enriched with the multivector_str,               │
 │       sieve_address, and a list of ClosestEmojiInfo (emoji character, category, and distance).                               │
 │    60                                                                                                                            │
 │    61 ### 2.7. RDF Ontology Generation (ontology_generator/mod.rs, process_function.rs, serialize.rs)                      │
 │    62                                                                                                                            │
 │    63 This final stage constructs the RDF graph and serializes it.                                                               │
 │    64 *   **Graph Construction**: The sophia RDF library is used to build an in-memory RDF graph (                             │
 │       sophia::inmem::graph::LightGraph).                                                                                       │
 │    65 *   **Namespace Definition**: Standard RDF, RDFS, and custom ex (example) and em (emoji) namespaces are defined.       │
 │    66 *   **Triple Insertion**: For each AnalyzedFunction, a set of RDF triples is generated and inserted into the graph.      │
 │       These triples link functions to their file paths, code snippets, semantic summaries, multivector embeddings, sieve         │
 │       addresses, and the details of their closest emojis.                                                                        │
 │    67 *   **Serialization**: The serialize_graph_to_file function serializes the constructed RDF graph into a Turtle (.ttl)  │
 │       file. It uses sophia_turtle with TurtleConfig to manage prefixes and ensure pretty-printing.                           │
 │    68                                                                                                                            │
 │    69 ## 3. Error Handling and Robustness                                                                                        │
 │    70                                                                                                                            │
 │    71 *   **`anyhow::Result`**: Extensive use of anyhow::Result for simplified error propagation throughout the pipeline.      │
 │    72 *   **File System Operations**: Errors during file reading, parsing, or writing are caught and logged, preventing crashes  │
 │       and allowing partial results.                                                                                              │
 │    73 *   **BERT Model Loading**: Handles potential errors during model and tokenizer loading from Hugging Face Hub.             │
 │    74                                                                                                                            │
 │    75 ## 4. Future Considerations                                                                                                │
 │    76                                                                                                                            │
 │    77 *   **Performance Optimization**: Further optimizations could include parallel processing of files, caching BERT           │
 │       embeddings for frequently encountered semantic summaries, and optimizing distance calculations for large emoji             │
 │       ontologies.                                                                                                                │
 │    78 *   **Semantic Summary Refinement**: The extract_semantic_summary function could be enhanced to produce more nuanced     │
 │       and comprehensive summaries of Rust functions, potentially using more advanced AST traversal and analysis techniques.      │
 │    79 *   **Customizable Emoji Ontology**: Allow users to provide their own emoji ontologies or extend the existing one.         │
 │    80 *   **Advanced Distance Metrics**: Explore more sophisticated distance metrics for multivectors beyond simple Euclidean    │
 │       distance.                                                                                                                  │
 │    81 *   **Error Handling for `unwrap()`**: Replace .unwrap() calls with proper error handling (e.g., ? operator or         │
 │       match statements) for increased robustness.                                                                              │

│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Core Extraction Process                                                                                                                 │
│    The markdown code extractor uses two main parsing functions to extract code snippets from different content formats:                    │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    1. Markdown Code Block Parser                                                                                                           │
│    The primary extraction function is extract_code_snippets which processes markdown-style triple-backtick code blocks using a state       │
│    machine approach extract.rs:25-74 . It iterates through each line, tracking whether it's inside or outside a code block, and when it    │
│    encounters closing backticks, it creates a CodeSnippet with metadata.                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    2. HTML Code Block Parser                                                                                                               │
│    For HTML content, extract_code_snippets_from_html uses the scraper crate to parse HTML documents and extract code from structured       │
│    elements with specific selectors extract_html.rs:11-55 . It looks for div[data-testid='markdown-code-block'] elements and extracts both │
│     language information and code content.                                                                                                 │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    User Interface Integration                                                                                                              │
│    The MarkdownCodeExtractor component orchestrates the entire process through several key handlers extractor.rs:23-59 :                   │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    File Upload: The upload_files handler processes files selected through the file input                                                   │
│    Drag &amp; Drop: The on_drop handler processes files dropped onto the interface                                                             │
│    Processing: Both methods call read_files which invokes process_file_engine to extract snippets                                          │
│    Processing Pipeline                                                                                                                     │
│    When files are processed, the system:                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Reads file content using the FileEngine extractor.rs:41-43                                                                              │
│    Calls the appropriate extraction function based on content type                                                                         │
│    Creates CodeSnippet objects with comprehensive metadata including content hash, token count, line count, and character count            │
│    extract.rs:77-100                                                                                                                       │
│    Updates the UI state through reactive signals to display results                                                                        │
│    Output and Management                                                                                                                   │
│    The extracted snippets are displayed through the FileDisplay component filedisplay.rs:10-46 , which renders individual code snippets    │
│    and provides clipboard functionality for copying extracted code.                                                                        │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Notes                                                                                                                                   │
│    The system supports both markdown files (.md, .markdown, .mdown) and HTML content containing markdown code blocks. The extraction       │
│    process is designed to handle various programming languages and provides comprehensive metadata for each extracted snippet. The UI uses │
│     Dioxus signals for reactive state management, ensuring the interface updates automatically as files are processed.                     │

│    Looking at your question about how memes orbit, you're asking about the orbital mechanics system in the solfunmeme-dioxus codebase,     │
│    specifically how meme entities move in orbital patterns within the visualization system.                                                │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Orbital Mechanics Implementation                                                                                                        │
│    The memes orbit through a sophisticated 4D orbital simulation system implemented in the ThemeOrbitalNetwork2 component                  │
│    solfunnice.rs:139-198 . Each meme is represented as a ThemeNode with physical properties including mass, position, and velocity.        │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    The orbital calculations use a 4D force model with Runge-Kutta 4th order integration orbits.rs:626-643 . The derivatives2 function      │
│    computes the gravitational forces in 4D space, where each meme experiences attraction toward the center based on its mass and distance. │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Visual Orbit Patterns                                                                                                                   │
│    The system creates three distinct orbital rings with different characteristics solfunnice.rs:142-162 :                                  │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Orbit 1: 300px diameter, 8-second rotation period                                                                                       │
│    Orbit 2: 500px diameter, 12-second period, reverse direction                                                                            │
│    Orbit 3: 700px diameter, 16-second period                                                                                               │
│    Each orbit contains meme nodes that follow circular paths with smooth CSS animations. The nodes have different visual properties and    │
│    hover effects solfunnice.rs:169-198 .                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Meme-Specific Orbital Behavior                                                                                                          │
│    Individual memes have unique orbital characteristics based on their properties from the MemeGenerator system meme_generator.rs:98-135 . │
│     Each meme has:                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    An emoji representation ( for functions,  for structs, etc.)                                                                           │
│    Mass-based orbital dynamics where higher-mass nodes have tighter orbits                                                                 │
│    Biosemiotic properties that influence their orbital behavior                                                                            │
│    The orbital paths are precomputed for performance and rendered as SVG paths, with nodes cycling through their orbits approximately      │
│    every 10 seconds at 60 FPS orbits.rs:610-614 .                                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Interactive Elements                                                                                                                    │
│    Memes retain interactivity while orbiting, including click handlers for spark effects and hover scaling orbits.rs:613 . The system also │
│     includes animated particles that spawn and move independently of the orbital system solfunnice.rs:446-489 .                            │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    Notes                                                                                                                                   │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    The orbital system is part of the larger SolFunNiceApp visualization framework and integrates with the meme ecosystem through the       │
│    ZeroOntologySystem. The 4D orbital mechanics provide a unique way to visualize code relationships and meme interactions in a dynamic,   │
│    physics-based environment.                                                                                                              │

╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯✦ Okay, I understand. You want the progress bar to show the current directory and progress. This means updating the progress bar's message
  dynamically during the analysis.  Since the analysis functions (analyze_project, analyze_markdown_files, analyze_project_tokens) are parallelized using rayon, directly
  updating a single ProgressBar from multiple threads can lead to race conditions and flickering. A more robust approach for parallel
  processing with indicatif is to use ProgressBar::for_each or ProgressBar::map with par_iter.  I will modify main.rs to pass the ProgressBar to the analysis functions. Then, in project_analyzer.rs, I will use pb.set_message()
  within the parallel processing loops to update the message with the current file being processed. This will provide a dynamic update,
  though some flickering might occur due to the nature of parallel updates.  Here's the plan:Modify prepare_sources/src/main.rs:Pass a clone of the ProgressBar to analyze_project, analyze_markdown_files, and analyze_project_tokens.</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1g7jtus r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">Modify prepare_sources/src/project_analyzer.rs:Update the signatures of analyze_project, analyze_markdown_files, and analyze_project_tokens to accept a pb: &amp;ProgressBar
parameter.
Inside the parallel processing loops, update the pb.set_message() with the current file path.</span></span></span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1adg3ll r-1x3r274 r-p1pxzi"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">  Let's start by modifying main.rs.

│    ### Step 2: Solana Account Structures                                                                                                   │
│    Each ontology is a Solana account, each instance is a transaction, and each transaction produces a new program. I’ll define account     │
│    structures using borsh for serialization, optimized for Solana’s 10KB limit.                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    #### Ontology Account                                                                                                                   │
│    Stores the ontology schema.                                                                                                             │
│                                                                                                                                            │

                                                                                │ │    use solana_program::pubkey::Pubkey;                                                                                                     │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │    #[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize, Debug, Clone)]                                                                               │ │    pub struct Ontology { </span><span></span><span class="token assign-left" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">PID</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(212, 212, 212);">=</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">$(</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">pgrep prepare_sources</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">)</span><span>
</span><span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(86, 156, 214);">if</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(212, 212, 212);">[</span><span> -n </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">"</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">$PID</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">"</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(212, 212, 212);">]</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(212, 212, 212);">;</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(86, 156, 214);">then</span><span>
</span><span>  </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(78, 201, 176);">echo</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">"Stopping existing prepare_sources process (PID: </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">$PID</span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">)..."</span><span>
</span><span>  </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(220, 220, 170);">kill</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(156, 220, 254);">$PID</span><span>
</span><span>  </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(220, 220, 170);">sleep</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(181, 206, 168);">2</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(106, 153, 85);"># Give it a moment to shut down</span><span>
</span><span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(86, 156, 214);">fi</span><span>
</span>
<span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(106, 153, 85);"># Build the latest release version</span><span>
</span><span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(78, 201, 176);">echo</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">"Building new release version..."</span><span>
</span>cargo build --release

<span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(106, 153, 85);"># Check if build was successful</span><span>

</span><span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(86, 156, 214);">fi</span><span>
</span>

</span><span></span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(78, 201, 176);">echo</span><span> </span><span class="token" style="color: rgb(206, 145, 120);">"Starting new prepare_sources instance..."</span><span>

</span>

│    2. Deploy an Ontology account to your validator.                                                                                      │
│    3. Create transactions for each instance (file, function, emoji, term).                                                                 │
│    4. Deploy a new Solana program per instance, which can host sub-accounts and transactions (recursive).                                  │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    #### Solana Program (Base Program)                                                                                                      │
│    This program manages the Ontology account and instance accounts.                                                                      │
│                                                                                                                                            │

│    #### Client-Side Bootstrapping Logic                                                                                                    │
│    Modify prepare_sources to connect to your validator and deploy the ontology and instances. Add to Cargo.toml:                       │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    toml                                                                                                                                 │ │    [dependencies]                                                                                                                          │ │    solana-client = "1.18"                                                                                                                  │ │    solana-sdk = "1.18"                                                                                                                     │ │    borsh = "0.10"                                                                                                                          │ │    serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }                                                                                      │ │                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    **Client Code** (src/solana_bootstrap.rs):                                                                                            │

                     │ │        let ontology_instruction = Instruction {                                                                                            │ │            program_id,                                                                                                                     │ │            accounts: vec![AccountMeta::new(ontology_pda, false), AccountMeta::new(payer.pubkey(), true)],                                  │ │            data: Instruction::CreateOntology {                                                                                             │ │                id: ontology.id,                                                                                                            │ │                classes: ontology.classes,                                                                                                  │ │                properties: ontology.properties,                                                                                            │ │            }.try_to_vec()?,                                                                                                                │ │        }; {                                                        │ │                    // Deploy term account and program                                                                                      │ │                }                                                                                                                           │ │            }                                                                                                                               │ │        }                                                                                                                                   │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │        Ok(())                                                                                                                              │ │    }                                                                                                                                       │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │    fn deploy_instance_program(                                                                                                             │ │        client: &amp;RpcClient,                                                                                                                 │ │        payer: &amp;Keypair,                                                                                                                    │ │        instance_pda: &amp;Pubkey,                                                                                                              │ │        instance_name: &amp;str,                                                                                                                │ │    ) -&gt; │    ### Step 4: Recursive Program Creation                                                                                                  │
│    Each instance transaction deploys a new Solana program (e.g., FunctionProgram_analyze_project). These programs can:                   │
│    - Host accounts (e.g., sub-terms or emojis).                                                                                            │
│    - Process transactions to create further programs (recursive).                                                                          │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    </span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">**Instance Program Template**</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">:                                                                                                          │
│    Each instance program follows a similar structure to the base program but is scoped to the instance. For example, the                   │
│    FunctionProgram_analyze_project might manage Term or ClosestEmojiInfo accounts related to analyze_project.                      │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    rust                                                                                                                                 │ │    use solana_program::{                                                                                                                   │ │        account_info::{next_account_info, AccountInfo},                                                                                     │ │        entrypoint,                                                                                                                         │ │        entrypoint::ProgramResult,                                                                                                          │ │        msg,                                                                                                                                │ │        program_error::ProgramError,                                                                                                        │ │        pubkey::Pubkey,                                                                                                                     │ │    };                                                                                                                                      │ │    use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};                                                                                          │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │    #[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize, Debug)]                                                                                      │ │    pub enum InstanceInstruction {                                                                                                          │ │        CreateSubTerm { text: String, description: String },                                                                                │ │        // Add other sub-instances as needed                                                                                                │ │    }                                                                                                                                       │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │    entrypoint!(process_instruction);                                                                                                       │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │    pub fn process_instruction(                                                                                                             │ │        program_id: &amp;Pubkey,                                                                                                                │ │        accounts: &amp;[AccountInfo],                                                                                                           │ │        instruction_data: &amp;[u8],                                                                                                            │ │    ) -&gt; ProgramResult {                                                                                                                    │ │        let instruction = InstanceInstruction::try_from_slice(instruction_data)?;                                                           │ │        let account_info_iter = &amp;mut accounts.iter();                                                                                       │ │        let sub_account = next_account_info(account_info_iter)?;                                                                            │ │                                                                                                                                            │ │        match instruction {                                                                                                                 │ │            InstanceInstruction::CreateSubTerm { text, description } =&gt; {                                                                   │ │                let term = Term {                                                                                                           │ │                    text,                                                                                                                   │ │                    description,                                                                                                            │ │                    emoji_refs: [Pubkey::default(); 8],                                                                                     │ │                    function_refs: [Pubkey::default(); 16],                                                                                 │ │                    ontology: *sub_account.owner, // Link to parent                                                                         │ │                    creator: *sub_account.owner,                                                                                            │ │                    timestamp: solana_program::clock::Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp,                                                         │ │                };                                                                                                                          │ │                term.serialize(&amp;mut &amp;mut sub_account.data.borrow_mut()[..])?;                                                               │ │                msg!("Created sub-term: {}", text);                                                                                         │ │                Ok(())                                                                                                                      │ │            }                                                                                                                               │ │        }                                                                                                                                   │ │    }                                                                                                                                       │ │                                                                                                                                         │

│    ### Step 5: Deployment Workflow                                                                                                         │
│    1. </span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">**Compile `prepare_sources`**</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">:                                                                                                       │
│       - Build the executable: cargo build --release.                                                                                     │
│       - Ensure Solana dependencies are included.                                                                                           │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    2. </span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">**Compile Solana Programs**</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">:                                                                                                         │
│       - Base program: cargo build-bpf --manifest-path=base_program/Cargo.toml.                                                           │
│       - Instance program templates: Generate a template for each instance type (e.g., function_program, file_program) and compile with │
│     cargo build-bpf.                                                                                                                     │
│                                                                                                                                            │
│    3. </span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">**Run `prepare_sources`**</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">:                                                                                                           │
│       - Update src/main.rs to include a bootstrap-solana command:                                                                      │
│    rust                                                                                                                                 │ │    if args[1] == "bootstrap-solana" {                                                                                                      │ │        let rdf_data = fs::read_to_string(&amp;args[2])?;                                                                                       │ │        let program_id = Pubkey::from_str(&amp;args[3])?;                                                                                       │ │        let payer = Keypair::from_base58_string(&amp;args[4])?;                                                                                 │ │        let rpc_url = "</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">http://localhost:8899</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">"; // Your validator RPC                                                                        │ │        solana_bootstrap::bootstrap_to_solana(&amp;rdf_data, program_id, &amp;payer, rpc_url)?;                                                     │ │    }                                                                                                                                       │ │                                                                                                                                         │
│                                                                                                                                            │

│    ### Step 3: Source Scanner and Buy Order Planning                                                                                       │
│    The </span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3">**Source Scanner**</span></span><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3 r-1x3r274"><span class="css-1jxf684 r-bcqeeo r-1ttztb7 r-qvutc0 r-poiln3"> in prepare_sources analyzes the RDF data to:                                                                   │
│    1. Extract instances (files, functions, emojis, terms).                                                                                 │

│    3. Write buy orders to the chain.                                                                                                       │

│    ### Step 5: Bootstrapping prepare_sources as Purchase Agent                                                                           │
│    The prepare_sources executable:                                                                                                       │
│    1. Parses RDF data to extract instances.                                                                                                │
│    2. Uses the Source Scanner to plan buy orders.                                                                                          │
│    3. Deploys the ontology, instances, and buy orders to the validator.                                                                    │
│    4. Creates a new program per buy order (recursive).                                                                                     │
